outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Primary LHON-causing mitochondrial DNA variants commonly affect MT-ND genes encoding subunits of respiratory-chain complex I, impairing NADH-to-ubiquinone electron transfer and mitochondrial ATP production in vulnerable retinal ganglion cells.
vignette: A 23-year-old man develops painless blurring of central vision in one eye followed several weeks later by similar visual loss in the other eye. Visual field testing shows dense central scotomas. His mother is unaffected, but two maternal uncles developed comparable vision loss as young adults.
lead: The most common pathogenic variants causing this disorder affect mitochondrial genes encoding subunits of which respiratory-chain complex?
distractor_notes: Complex II transfers electrons from succinate/FADH2 to ubiquinone. The major LHON mtDNA genes MT-ND1, MT-ND4, MT-ND4L, and MT-ND6 encode complex I subunits, not complex II.
Complex III accepts electrons from ubiquinol and transfers them to cytochrome c; the canonical LHON MT-ND genes are not complex III subunits.
Complex IV transfers electrons from cytochrome c to oxygen; primary LHON-causing MT-ND variants instead principally disrupt complex I.
Complex V uses the proton gradient to synthesize ATP but is not the respiratory-chain complex encoded by the major LHON-associated MT-ND genes.
key_expl: The young-adult onset of bilateral painless subacute central visual loss plus maternal-line transmission is characteristic of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy. The common LHON-causing mitochondrial genes MT-ND1, MT-ND4, MT-ND4L, and MT-ND6 encode subunits of respiratory-chain complex I. Complex I accepts electrons from NADH and transfers them to ubiquinone while contributing to the proton gradient used for ATP synthesis.
objective: Recognize the maternal inheritance and bilateral central optic neuropathy of LHON and link its common MT-ND mutations to mitochondrial respiratory-chain complex I dysfunction.
clues: young adult with painless subacute bilateral central visual loss

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes LHON as central vision loss beginning commonly in teens or twenties, caused by mitochondrial MT-ND1, MT-ND4, MT-ND4L, or MT-ND6 variants, and inherited through mitochondrial DNA in a maternal pattern.
